title: Agentic Test-Time Training: Adapting Mid-Episode
hook: LLM agents degrade over long episodes, repeating failed moves — this method updates the model's weights continuously during the episode itself, but only on genuinely new information.
key_points: LLM agents on long trajectories revisit explored states and repeat failed actions, losing strategies that worked earlier.
aTTT reweights the training loss token-by-token: tokens that repeat across prior updates get downweighted, novel tokens stay fully weighted.
Repeated n-grams in update text signal the agent is stuck and training on them would amplify drift, not fix it.
Runs inside live episodes via vLLM's runtime LoRA API, at 1.9x the cost of not doing test-time training.
Improves success up to 5.0 points on ALFWorld and 4.9 points on SWE-bench Lite — mostly by preserving competence the model already had over long trajectories.
content_html: Long-running LLM agents have a quiet failure mode: as an episode stretches on, they start repeating actions that already failed, or forget approaches that worked minutes earlier. Test-time training (TTT) — updating weights on the fly — sounds like a fix, but naively retraining on a stuck agent's own repetitive output just reinforces the rut.
extra_html: The authors study continuous TTT inside multi-turn agent episodes, where each update reshapes the policy that generates all later training text — a self-training loop that helps when genuinely new trajectory information shows up, but can spiral when the agent is stuck and keeps training on similar text. Their fix, Agentic Test-Time Training (aTTT), reweights the loss at the token level: tokens that recur across a window of prior updates get downweighted, while novel tokens keep full weight, since update-text repetition is exactly the signal that distinguishes "learning something new" from "amplifying drift." To make this practical inside a live episode, they built a concurrent serving system on vLLM's runtime LoRA API, adding only 1.9x overhead. The result: up to 5.0 points on ALFWorld and 4.9 on SWE-bench Lite, concentrated in cases where the model already had the competence but drifted away from using it over a long trajectory. Yanbo Wang and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: Plans Don't Persist: Context Management Is Load-Bearing for Agents
related.hook: An agent writes a plan, then context compression evicts it. This paper shows the plan never became internal state — once it leaves the window, the agent forgets it and task success craters.

flashcards.prompt: What failure mode does agentic test-time training (aTTT) target?
flashcards.back_html: LLM agents drifting over long episodes — revisiting explored states, repeating failed actions, and losing strategies that worked earlier in the trajectory.

flashcards.prompt: How does aTTT decide which tokens to downweight during its continuous mid-episode updates?

choices.text: Tokens that appear in repeated n-grams from prior updates are downweighted, since repetition signals the agent is stuck
It downweights the most recent tokens to avoid overfitting to the last action
It randomly drops half the tokens in every update
It downweights tokens the model is most confident about

flashcards.explanation_html: Repeated n-grams across updates signal the agent revisiting the same failed text, so training fully on it would amplify drift. Novel tokens — genuinely new trajectory information — stay fully weighted.
